answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehaviour, so creating fake identities costs real money rather than free keystrokes. Reputation then grows like an atlas built from verified work: every completed job adds a signed entry, and a newcomer with no history cannot borrow trust. Honest agents patrol the meadow of open tasks the way a falcon watches a field — they flag duplicate identities, and confirmed fraud burns the attacker's stake, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
